meaningEn: Basic plain present tense declaration for action verbs.
meaningId: Bentuk deklaratif datar waktu sekarang untuk kata kerja aksi.

notesEn.formation: Verb Stem + ~는다 (if stem ends in consonant) / ~ㄴ다 (if stem ends in vowel).
notesEn.usage: Used in written Korean, plain/impersonal declarations, diaries, news, or informal self-talk.
notesEn.nuance: This is the non-polite plain form (해라체/plain form). Do not confuse with honorific/polite endings like ~아/어/해요 or ~습니다.

notesId.formation: Katak Dasar Kata Kerja + ~는다 (jika akhiran konsonan) / ~ㄴ다 (jika akhiran vokal).
notesId.usage: Digunakan dalam tulisan bahasa Korea, deklarasi polos/impersonal, diari, berita, atau berbicara sendiri.
notesId.nuance: Ini adalah bentuk polos tidak resmi (해라체/plain form). Jangan tertukar dengan akhiran sopan seperti ~아/어/해요 atau ~습니다.

quiz.question: How do you conjugate the verb '읽다' (to read) into the plain present tense form?
quiz.explanationEn: The verb stem 읽 ends in a consonant, so ~는다 is attached -> 읽는다.
quiz.explanationId: Katas dasar 읽 berakhiran konsonan, sehingga ~는다 ditempelkan -> 읽는다.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: I go to school. -> 나는 학교에 가___.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: The stem 가 ends in a vowel, so attach ~ㄴ다.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Kata dasar 가 berakhiran vokal, jadi tempelkan ~ㄴ다.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean plain present tense: 'I eat rice.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea bentuk polos sekarang: 'Saya makan nasi.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use 나는 + rice (밥) + object particle 을 + 먹다 conjugated with ~는다.
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan 나는 + nasi (밥) + partikel objek 을 + 먹다 yang dikonjugasi dengan ~는다.

notesEn.formation: If stem vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ -> add ~아요. Otherwise -> add ~어요. If stem ends in 하다 -> becomes 해요.
notesEn.usage: The most standard daily spoken Korean ending for polite, friendly conversation.
notesEn.nuance: Essential standard polite style (해요체). Used when speaking to acquaintances, colleagues, or strangers politely.

notesId.formation: Jika vokal kata dasar ㅏ atau ㅗ -> tambahkan ~아요. Selain itu -> tambahkan ~어요. Jika berakhiran 하다 -> menjadi 해요.
notesId.usage: Akhiran bahasa Korea lisan harian paling standar untuk percakapan sopan dan ramah.
notesId.nuance: Gaya sopan standar yang sangat penting (해요체). Digunakan saat berbicara dengan kenalan, rekan kerja, atau orang asing secara sopan.

quiz.question: What is the ~아/어/해요 form of the verb '공부하다' (to study)?
quiz.explanationEn: Verbs ending in 하다 always conjugate to 해요 in the informal polite style.
quiz.explanationId: Kata kerja berakhiran 하다 selalu dikonjugasikan menjadi 해요 dalam gaya sopan informal.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: I meet a friend. -> 친구를 만나___.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: 만나다 already contains ㅏ, so adding ~아요 merges into 만나 + 요.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: 만나다 sudah mengandung ㅏ, jadi penambahan ~아요 melebur menjadi 만나 + 요.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean (informal polite): 'I eat an apple.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea (sopan informal): 'Saya makan apel.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use 저는 + apple (사과) + object particle 를 + 먹다 conjugated as 먹어요.
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan 저는 + apel (사과) + partikel objek 를 + 먹다 yang dikonjugasi menjadi 먹어요.

notesEn.formation: Verb Stem + ~ㅂ니다 (if stem ends in vowel) / ~습니다 (if stem ends in consonant).
notesEn.usage: Used in official announcements, news broadcasts, business presentations, and military settings.
notesEn.nuance: Highly polite and formal (하십시오체). Adds deference and professional distance.

notesId.formation: Kata Dasar Kata Kerja + ~ㅂ니다 (jika akhiran vokal) / ~습니다 (jika akhiran konsonan).
notesId.usage: Digunakan dalam pengumuman resmi, siaran berita, presentasi bisnis, dan lingkungan militer.
notesId.nuance: Sangat sopan dan formal (하십시오체). Menambahkan rasa hormat dan jarak profesional.

quiz.question: How do you conjugate '가다' (to go) into the formal polite present tense?
quiz.explanationEn: The stem 가 ends in a vowel, so ~ㅂ니다 attaches directly beneath it to form 갑니다.
quiz.explanationId: Kata dasar 가 berakhiran vokal, sehingga ~ㅂ니다 menempel langsung di bawahnya membentuk 갑니다.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: I learn Korean (formal). -> 저는 한국어를 배우___.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: 배우다 stem ends in vowel ㅜ, attach ~ㅂ니다 underneath.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Kata dasar 배우다 berakhiran vokal ㅜ, tempelkan ~ㅂ니다 di bawahnya.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to formal Korean: 'I go to school.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea formal: 'Saya pergi ke sekolah.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use 저는 + school (학교) + particle 에 + 가다 conjugated with ~ㅂ니다.
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan 저는 + sekolah (학교) + partikel 에 + 가다 yang dikonjugasi dengan ~ㅂ니다.

notesEn.formation: Noun + 을 (if ends in consonant) / 를 (if ends in vowel).
notesEn.usage: Marks the direct object that receives the action of a transitive verb.
notesEn.nuance: Essential for transitive action verbs. Omitted in casual spoken conversation when clear from context.

notesId.formation: Kata Benda + 을 (jika berakhiran konsonan) / 를 (jika berakhiran vokal).
notesId.usage: Menandai objek langsung yang menerima tindakan dari kata kerja transitif.
notesId.nuance: Sangat penting untuk kata kerja aksi transitif. Sering dihilangkan dalam percakapan santai jika konteksnya sudah jelas.

quiz.question: Which object particle attaches to '밥' (rice/food)?
quiz.explanationEn: 밥 ends in a final consonant (ㅂ), so it takes the object particle ~을.
quiz.explanationId: 밥 berakhiran konsonan akhir (ㅂ), jadi menggunakan partikel objek ~을.

fillInTheBlank.hintEn: 차 ends in a vowel (ㅏ), so attach ~를.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'I read a book.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Saya membaca buku.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use book (책) + object particle 을 + read (읽어요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan buku (책) + partikel objek 을 + membaca (읽어요).

meaningEn: Action taking place at a location.
meaningId: Aksi/kegiatan yang terjadi di suatu lokasi.

notesEn.usage: Indicates the physical place where a dynamic action or activity is performed.
notesEn.nuance: Contrast with ~에: ~에 indicates destination or existence (가다, 오다, 있다), whereas ~에서 indicates active dynamic events taking place (공부하다, 먹다, 일하다).

notesId.formation: Kata Benda Lokasi + 에서 + Kata Kerja Aksi.
notesId.usage: Menunjukkan tempat fisik di mana suatu tindakan atau aktivitas dinamis dilakukan.
notesId.nuance: Beda dengan ~에: ~에 menunjukkan tujuan atau keberadaan (가다, 오다, 있다), sedangkan ~에서 menunjukkan aktivitas dinamis yang sedang berlangsung (공부하다, 먹다, 일하다).

examples.meaningEn: I eat rice at a restaurant.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly says 'I study at the library'?
quiz.explanationEn: Because '공부하다' is an active dynamic verb, the location particle ~에서 must be used.
quiz.explanationId: Karena '공부하다' adalah kata kerja aksi dinamis, partikel lokasi ~에서 harus digunakan.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: I rest at home. -> 집___ 쉬어요.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Resting is an active state/event taking place at home, so use ~에서.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Beristirahat adalah aktivitas yang berlangsung di rumah, jadi gunakan ~에서.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'I study at the library.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Saya belajar di perpustakaan.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use library (도서관) + location particle 에서 + study (공부해요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan perpustakaan (도서관) + partikel lokasi 에서 + belajar (공부해요).
